To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of ET-1 and its receptor is increased in cirrhosis, while ET-3 and its receptor are decreased in liver adenocarcinoma.
ETs and their ET-1 receptors were found in normal liver, and were increased in cirrhotics.

(1) Endothelin-1 (ET-1) and ET-3 are present in the liver, (2) The expression of ET-1 and its receptor is increased in liver cirrhosis, (3) Hepatocellular carcinoma shows increased ET-1 expression compared to normal liver, but the expression of ET-3 is decreased, (4) Fibrolamellar carcinoma shows increased expression of both ET-1, and ET-3 as compared to normal liver
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the ET system in liver disease.
the localization and expression of ET-1, -3, and their receptors in the liver.
the expression of endothelins and their endothelin receptors in cirrhostic and neoplasitic human liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ETs are involved in cirrhotogenesis and neoplastic transformation.
ET-1 and -3 are present in the normal liver and that cirrhosis and HCCs show alterations in the expression of these peptides.
the expression of ETs and ET-receptors is altered in cirrhosis, FLCs, and Ads.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in HCC, there is a decrease in immunoreactivity of ET-1 and an increase in ET-3.
ET-1 and/or ET-3 are up-regulated in cirrhotics, FLCs and Ads, and ET receptors are up-regulated, particularly in cirrhosis, but down-regulated in Ads.
ETs are increased in cirrhosis, while their receptors are decreased in HCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are significant differences in the expression of the endothelin axis in the different liver diseases.
ET-1 and its receptors may be involved in the pathogenesis of cirrhosis and HCC, and may be useful as therapeutic targets.
the immunoreactivity for ETs is not increased in HCCs.
